title: External products respect Segal and coefficient equivalences
statement: Use the Segal-presheaf notation and the fixed-endpoint coefficient localization of [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization]. Let $C,D$ be small monoidal infinity categories. If $f:X\to X'$ is a Segal equivalence in $P(C_\otimes)$ and $Y\in P(D_\otimes)$ is any presheaf, then $f\boxtimes\mathrm{id}_Y$ is a Segal equivalence in $P((C\times D)_\otimes)$; the analogous assertion holds with the variables interchanged. If $X\in Q_C$ and $Y\in Q_D$, then $X\boxtimes Y\in Q_{C\times D}$. For monoidally compatible small sets $S\subset\operatorname{Ar}(P(C))$, $T\subset\operatorname{Ar}(P(D))$, if $f:X\to X'$ is an $S$-local Segal equivalence between Segal presheaves and $Y\in Q_D$, then $f\boxtimes\mathrm{id}_Y$ is an $S\odot T$-local Segal equivalence. If $X\in Q_C$ and $g:Y\to Y'$ is a $T$-local Segal equivalence, then $\mathrm{id}_X\boxtimes g$ is an $S\odot T$-local Segal equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 4.10; Corollaries 7.5-7.6; fixed-endpoint reconstruction of Lemma 8.11 and Corollaries 8.13-8.14 after the correction of Observations 8.6-8.7 recorded in report.md. Agent reconstruction; no Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: First establish the labelled inner-horn facts needed below. Let $W_C$ be the class inverted by $L_C$. The localization model and the saturation theorem identify $W_C$ with the strongly saturated class generated by labelled spine inclusions. Induct on the horn dimension $n\geq2$. For $n=2$ the inner horn is the spine, so its inclusion lies in $W_C$. If all inner horns of dimension less than $n$ lie in $W_C$, the finite lower-dimensional filtration of [lem-coef-labelled-spine-prism-horn-calculus] shows that the map from the spine to $\Lambda^n_i(\boldsymbol c)$ lies in $W_C$. Its composite with the horn inclusion is a spine inclusion, so two-out-of-three puts the horn inclusion in $W_C$. Thus all labelled inner horns, and consequently all maps in their weakly saturated class, are Segal equivalences. For the latter assertion, pushouts and retracts are already closure operations of $W_C$. For a continuous ordinal sequence of arrows in $W_C$, transfinite induction puts each map from the initial stage to a later stage in $W_C$: the initial case is an identity, a successor uses composition, and a nonzero limit stage takes the arrow colimit of those maps with constant source. This proves closure under transfinite composition. The induction was for any small monoidal category, so it also proves these assertions for $D$ and $C\times D$. The labelled spine inclusions themselves are inner anodyne by the cited horn calculus.

Fix a labelled horn inclusion $h:\Lambda^n_i(\boldsymbol c)\to\Delta^n(\boldsymbol c)$ of $C_\otimes$. We prove, by induction on $m\geq0$, that $h\boxtimes\Delta^m(\boldsymbol d)$ is a Segal equivalence for every list $\boldsymbol d\in D^m$. At $m=0$ the vertex formula in [lem-coef-labelled-spine-prism-horn-calculus] identifies this map with the horn labelled by $(c_j,\mathbf1_D)$; step 1 applies. Suppose the assertion holds for all dimensions less than $m$. The labelled boundary is the colimit of its proper labelled faces and their intersections, all of lower dimension, by that same node. The external product preserves small colimits in each variable: evaluate its defining product formula, use pointwise presheaf colimits and separate colimit preservation by products of spaces from the model node. Closure of Segal equivalences under arrow colimits therefore shows that $h\boxtimes\partial\Delta^m(\boldsymbol d)$ is a Segal equivalence. Factor $h\boxtimes\Delta^m(\boldsymbol d)$ through
$$U=(\Lambda^n_i(\boldsymbol c)\boxtimes\Delta^m(\boldsymbol d))\amalg_{\Lambda^n_i(\boldsymbol c)\boxtimes\partial\Delta^m(\boldsymbol d)}(\Delta^n(\boldsymbol c)\boxtimes\partial\Delta^m(\boldsymbol d)).$$
The first map is a pushout of the boundary equivalence. The second, $U\to\Delta^n(\boldsymbol c)\boxtimes\Delta^m(\boldsymbol d)$, is the inner-anodyne boundary–horn prism map of the cited calculus, hence a Segal equivalence by step 1. Their composite proves the induction step.

source.place: Corollaries 7.4-7.5: explicit induction on the passive simplex dimension

proof.text: Every presheaf $Y\in P(D_\otimes)$ is a small colimit of labelled representables by [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density]. Separate cocontinuity of the external product, proved pointwise in step 2, and closure of local equivalences under colimits extend step 2 to $h\boxtimes\mathrm{id}_Y$ for every labelled inner horn $h$. For fixed $Y$, the functor $-\boxtimes Y$ preserves pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Consequently it sends every labelled inner-anodyne map to a Segal equivalence, and in particular sends every labelled spine inclusion to a Segal equivalence by step 1. The class of maps sent to Segal equivalences is strongly saturated: two-out-of-three and retracts are preserved by any functor, and pushouts and small arrow colimits are preserved here by separate cocontinuity. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] to the labelled-spine localization to conclude that $f\boxtimes\mathrm{id}_Y$ is a Segal equivalence for every Segal equivalence $f$. For the other variable, present a fixed $X\in P(C_\otimes)$ as a small colimit of labelled representables. The exchanged-factor boundary–horn prism and vertex formulas give the induction of step 2 for each horn of $D_\otimes$ with each such passive representable. Separate cocontinuity and density give $\mathrm{id}_X\boxtimes h$ for every labelled horn $h$ of $D_\otimes$. Its closure under weak saturation covers the labelled spines, and its closure under strong saturation covers every Segal equivalence of $D_\otimes$. Reordering the factors in the product of spaces identifies the exchanged formulas with this second-variable external product.

source.place: Corollaries 7.5-7.6: Yoneda density, weak saturation, then strong saturation

proof.text:
For $X\in Q_C$ and $Y\in Q_D$, the Segal comparison for $X\boxtimes Y$ is the product of their two Segal comparisons. Explicitly its target is
$$\bigl(X([1](c_1))\times Y([1](d_1))\bigr)\times_{X([0])\times Y([0])}\cdots\times_{X([0])\times Y([0])}\bigl(X([1](c_n))\times Y([1](d_n))\bigr),$$
which identifies with the product of the corresponding iterated fibre products in $X$ and $Y$ by the universal property of a pullback. Its source is $X([n](\boldsymbol c))\times Y([n](\boldsymbol d))$. Both factor comparisons are equivalences by the definition of $Q_C,Q_D$, so their product is an equivalence. This proves that $X\boxtimes Y$ is Segal, including arbitrary empty or disconnected vertex spaces.

source.place: Lemma 4.10: direct calculation of the Segal comparison

proof.text: Here is the coefficient calculation, independently of algebroid colimits. Write $R:P(C\times D)\to P^{S\odot T}(C\times D)$ for the coefficient reflector supplied by the model node, and $\mu(A,B)(c,d)=A(c)\times B(d)$ for the external product of coefficient presheaves. Pointwise colimits of presheaves are supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], and cartesian product of spaces preserves small colimits separately by the model node; thus $\mu$ preserves small colimits separately. Fix $d\in D$. The class of arrows $u$ for which $R\mu(u,y(d))$ is an equivalence is strongly saturated: $R\mu(-,y(d))$ preserves colimits, since $R$ has the inclusion as right adjoint and hence preserves small colimits by [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints], and equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three and are stable under retracts and colimits. The class contains $S$ by the defining generators $s\boxtimes y(d)$ of $S\odot T$. Hence it contains every $S$-local coefficient equivalence by the saturation theorem. For arbitrary $B\in P(D)$, express $B$ as a small colimit of $y(d)$ by Yoneda density. Taking this colimit in both ends of $u\boxtimes B$ proves that $R\mu(u,B)$ is an equivalence whenever $u$ is an $S$-local coefficient equivalence. For the second variable fix $c\in C$. The colimit-preserving functor $R\mu(y(c),-)$ inverts each $t\in T$ by the generators $y(c)\boxtimes t$. Its inverse image of equivalences is strongly saturated by the same listed closure operations, so the saturation theorem makes it invert every $T$-local coefficient equivalence $v$. Express arbitrary $A\in P(C)$ as its Yoneda colimit and apply separate cocontinuity to both ends; this proves that $R\mu(A,v)$ is an equivalence. This includes initial presheaves and empty density diagrams.

source.place: Definition 8.1 and Lemma 8.3; agent reconstruction of the coefficient-generator calculation using density and saturation

proof.text:
Let $f:X\to X'$ be an $S$-local Segal equivalence with $X,X'\in Q_C$, and fix $Y\in Q_D$. The corrected model node states that $L_C^S$ retains the object space and applies the coefficient reflector to every mapping presheaf. Since $L_C^Sf$ is an equivalence, its map on object spaces, which is $f_0:X([0])\to X'([0])$, is an equivalence. Moreover, for every pair $x,x'\in X([0])$, the induced map
$$u_{x,x'}:H_X(x,x')\longrightarrow H_{X'}(f_0x,f_0x')$$
is an $S$-local coefficient equivalence, because its coefficient reflection is the mapping-object map of $L_C^Sf$. For $y,y'\in Y([0])$, the definition of the mapping fibre and the formula for $\boxtimes$ give
$$H_{X\boxtimes Y}((x,y),(x',y'))\simeq H_X(x,x')\boxtimes H_Y(y,y').$$
This identity follows by taking the fibre of the product of the two edge-to-endpoint maps. By step 4 both product presheaves are Segal. Apply $L_{C\times D}^{S\odot T}$. Its mapping-object map is the coefficient reflection of $u_{x,x'}\boxtimes H_Y(y,y')$, an equivalence by step 5; its object-space map is $f_0\times\mathrm{id}_{Y([0])}$, an equivalence. Thus the resulting algebroid map under the model equivalence is fully faithful with equivalent object spaces. It is an equivalence by [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve], applied to the presentably monoidal coefficient category $P^{S\odot T}(C\times D)$ supplied by the model node. This proves the first coefficient-local clause. If instead $X\in Q_C$ and $g:Y\to Y'$ is a $T$-local Segal equivalence, its object map is an equivalence and its mapping-presheaf maps $v_{y,y'}$ are $T$-local coefficient equivalences by the same reflector formula. Use the second-variable calculation of step 5 on $H_X(x,x')\boxtimes v_{y,y'}$; the resulting reflected map has equivalent objects and is fully faithful, so the same equivalence criterion proves the last clause.

The item's statement and stmt_deps are word for word the live side DAG's, so no target is weakened. All citations are in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, tool_uses is empty, there is no cycle, and proof_deps equals the union of the uses. Haugseng arXiv:2311.13362 is not in literature/ (the worker reported it as WANTED), so I checked the new node lem-coef-labelled-spine-prism-horn-calculus directly. (1) Labelled faces are lower-dimensional labelled representables, because C_⊗→Δ is a cartesian fibration and pullback commutes with colimits. The boundary is the ∞-colimit of its faces because each poset of faces containing a given image is contractible; m=1 gives v⊔v and m=0 gives ∅. (2) The spine-to-Λ^n_i filtration by pushouts along injective inner horns of dimension at most n−1 was found by a script search for every 0<i<n with n≤6; n=2 is empty. (3) The prism clause is the colimit-preserving labelled pullback applied to the ordinary pushout-product, which is the Mathlib leaf lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product. (4) The vertex formula holds because Hom_{D_⊗}([k](d'),[0]) = ∏Map(d'_j,1), so Δ^n(c)⊠v ≃ Δ^n(c,1). The node is not a duplicate of the ordinary cbc or coef nodes and does not restate the item.
